findings.description: tsconfig.json sets sourceMap: true, and tsc writes each .map's `sources` relative to the map's own folder. Compiling into .pup-build.X/dist/ (one level deeper than dist/) gives `../../../src/...`. After the move to dist/, every shipped source map points one folder above the repo.
findings.body:
**Every emitted source map points one folder too high after the swap**

`tsconfig.build.json` inherits `"sourceMap": true` from `tsconfig.json`, and neither file sets `sourceRoot`, `mapRoot` or `inlineSources`. tsc writes each map's `sources` relative to the folder the map file is in:

- Before this PR, `dist/cli/index.js.map` held `"../../src/cli/index.ts"`.
- Now the map is written at `.pup-build.Ab12cd/dist/cli/index.js.map`, one level deeper, so it holds `"../../../src/cli/index.ts"`.
- The `mv` on line 32 moves it to `dist/cli/index.js.map` without changing it. From there the path resolves to `<repo>/../src/cli/index.ts`, which does not exist.

**Trigger:** any `pnpm build`, followed by `node --enable-source-maps dist/cli/index.js ...` or a debugger attached to the installed `pup`. Stack traces and breakpoints then map to missing files, and nothing reports an error. `pup` itself never loads the maps, but `package.json` has no `files` field, so they ship with the package.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/c7cb47ed3afee6c7cf0a16c461ec8919399e1bb9/scripts/build.sh#L18

**Fix:** emit at the same depth as `dist/`. Pass `--outDir "$STAGE"` so the `mktemp -d ./.pup-build.XXXXXX` directory is the output folder itself, then `mv "$STAGE" dist`. Park the previous `dist/` somewhere other than inside `$STAGE`, for example a second `mktemp -d` directory that the EXIT trap also removes.

(Medium confidence: this follows tsc's documented source-map path behaviour, but a static review could not run a build to check it.)

findings.description: The doc still calls `pnpm build` "a bare `tsc`", but it now runs `bash scripts/build.sh`, which type-checks, compiles into a staging dir and swaps the result into dist/. The point that nothing rewrites specifiers still holds; only the wording is stale.

The 100-iteration mkdir lock loop (with LOCKED and the second trap) only matters when two builds share one dist/, and each worktree has its own. A SIGKILLed build leaves .pup-build.lock behind, and every later build then waits 10s and fails until someone removes it by hand. Consider dropping the lock, or using a single `mkdir "$LOCK" || exit 1`.

The `[ ! -L "$STAGE" ]` check can never fire: `mktemp -d` creates the directory itself (exclusively), so it cannot return a symlink, and a planted symlink at that name makes mktemp fail instead. Delete the line.
Header line 3 (`pnpm build -> type-checks, compiles into a fresh directory, then swaps it in`) restates the script body. Lines 2, 4 and 5 carry the real WHY, so line 3 can go.

refuted_findings.description: The per-run staging dir ./.pup-build.XXXXXX sits in the worktree but is not gitignored. A session's Bash calls that finish while a build is running see about 340 untracked files there, which is over pup's scope re-check cap of 200, so those calls are refused. Before this change, build output only went to the gitignored dist/.
refuted_findings.refutation: The `.gitignore` entry `dist/` has no leading or middle slash, so git matches a `dist` directory at any depth. tsc's output in `./.pup-build.XXXXXX/dist/` is therefore ignored, and the scope re-check's `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` (src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts:1047) runs without `--ignored`, so it never sees it. The only untracked content is the old dist/ moved to `$STAGE/old`, which exists only for the few milliseconds between the renames and the EXIT trap. `.pup-build.lock` is an empty directory, which git status never lists. So neither the 200-path cap nor the merged worktree-clean concern about a SIGKILLed build is realistically reachable.
